name: Gundi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: Like all known Mundu-Baka members, Ngundi is a tone language. It features three lexical register tones, namely high (H), mid (M), and low (L). High tone is marked by ´, low tone by `, whilst mid tone is diacritically unmarked. [...] Contour tones occur only on long vowels or diphthongs, suggesting the mora as the tone-bearing unit. VV-sequences and thus contour tones are scarce. [...] Ngundi features four syllable types of which CV is the most frequent. [...] Closed syllables do not exist.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ngundi is described as a three-level register-tone language (H/M/L, mora as TBU); the only existing description says nothing about word stress or accent, so no stress rule can be stated.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on (mostly CV) syllables/morae; word shapes CV to CV.CV.CV(.CV). No statement about word- or phrase-level prominence.
new_statements.identity_note: Winkhart 2025 describes Ngundi (ISO gdi, glottocode gund1247), the Ubangi/Mundu-Baka language closely related to Baka and Limassa, from ca. 25 speakers at Seke and Thanry (Likouala, Rep. Congo). His fn. 1 warns it is NOT the Bantu C10 language Ngundi [ndn] spoken in the same area; older sources (Ouzilleau 1911) call it 'Gundi (sur la Bodingue)'. The single Glottolog 5.1 'grammar_sketch' ref (Balep, 'bakaa') is a computerized mis-assignment and not about this language.

sources.note: Sec. 2 Phonology (pp. 342-344) covers phoneme inventory, tone (2.2: tone language, three register tones H/M/L, contour tones only on VV, mora as TBU) and phonotactics (only open syllables). No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the 11-page sketch (grep of full text: zero hits for stress/accent/prominence).
